name: CAPS MENTAL HEALTH GROUPS SPRING 2026
description:
Led by our licensed clinicians, our groups and support spaces help you improve your relationships, learn about yourself and others, enhance your communication skills, and reduce isolation within a supportive, normalizing environment of peers.

Group Counseling

At CAPS, we offer group therapy as a valuable opportunity for self-discovery and addressing concerns in a supportive and collaborative environment. Our group sessions typically consist of 4-10 students who meet weekly throughout the semester, all under the expert guidance of our CAPS clinicians. Joining a group allows you to gain valuable insights into yourself and others, fostering personal growth and understanding in a nurturing setting.

name: SENIOR WEEK: Last Night
description: It’s the last night, and you won’t want to miss out! This year's Last Night tradition is bigger and better: bring your friends and families to enjoy our margarita bar, arcade games, and more! Let's close out Senior Week with the best night yet!

name: CAPS Presents: The Next Phase: a Support-Focused Group for Students Who Will Soon Graduate
description: This group is for both undergraduate and graduate school students who are nearing graduation and preparing for the next chapters in their lives. It is a peer support space where students have an opportunity to share their affective and cognitive experiences regarding their futures. This mutual disclosure and exploration is intended to help normalize the students' experiences and facilitate support, encouragement and helpful reflection and feedback.

name: SENIOR WEEK: First-Gen Senior Class Photo

This event offers graduating seniors a chance to come together for a large group photo to commemorate their time at GW and celebrate their achievements alongside their peers. This will serve as a meaningful keepsake for students as they prepare to graduate and reflect on their journey.

name: SENIOR WEEK: First-Gen Senior Photos
description:
Celebrate your achievement as a first-generation college graduate with professional graduation portraits! Join us for the First-Gen Graduation Photos event, where graduating seniors will have the opportunity to take professional photos in their cap and gown, as well as an additional outfit of their choice. Students will be able to take one photo in their graduation attire and one in an outfit of their choice, so we encourage them to have both ready for their scheduled time slot. This is a great opportunity to celebrate your journey, represent your first-gen identity, and create lasting memories as you prepare to graduate.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: Movie Night in Georgetown: 'Michael' @AMC Georgetown 14
description:
Michael is a 2026 American musical biographical drama film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by John Logan.

It follows the life of American singer Michael Jackson, covering the period from his involvement in the Jackson 5 in the 60s to his early solo career. Jackson is portrayed by his nephew Jaafar Jackson in his film debut.

The ensemble cast includes Nia Long, Laura Harrier, Juliano Krue Valdi, Miles Teller, and Colman Domingo.

The music.

The moments.

The legacy that moved the world. In partnership with Lionsgate, BET takes you back to the performances that defined a generation—and still hit just as hard today.

From the first note to the final move, Michael Jackson didn’t just perform… he created moments we all remember.

MONDAY, April 27th 

We will be traveling to AMC Georgetown 14. 

Will be meeting in the lobby Guthridge Hall @6:30pm. 

Movie Starts @7:10pm.  Run time is 127 minutes.  

Tickets are on us. Your ride there and back in on us. 

Popcorn, Soda Pop, & Candy on you! 

First some, First serve. So RSVP Soon.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: FPP's 9 to 5
location: Blackbox Theatre, B2 Level West Hall MVC
description:
Forbidden Planet Productions presents 9 to 5, directed by Devika Mukherjee, with Teresa Seraphin, Jai Gough, Lila Trout, Jacob Khabie, and Narissa AlDayaa! Set in the late 1970s, this high-energy musical follows three coworkers who band together to take control of their toxic workplace and turn the tables on their sexist boss. Packed with humor, heart, and music by Dolly Parton, it’s a story of friendship, revenge, and empowerment in a man’s world. Join us this weekend for a bold, hilarious, and feel-good night at the theater!

 

📅 April 23rd @ 8:00pm; April 24th @ 6:30pm and 9:30pm; and April 25th @ 6:30pm and 9:30pm!
📍 Blackbox Theater, B2 Level West Hall - Mount Vernon Campus

Tickets will go live Tuesday, 4/21 at 8 pm: https://go.gwu.edu/fpptickets. Tickets for this event are $5 each, paid in cash or via Venmo at the door. Please arrive at least 10 minutes before the posted show time, or your presale ticket will be released to those waiting for a door ticket. 

This show contains themes of sexual harassment, adult situations, mild profanity, suggestive humor, weapons use, alcohol use, and violence.

 

Accessibility: While the West Hall Blackbox is an accessible space, the Mount Vernon Campus is partially accessible. Please reach out to fpp@gwu.edu or christopher.gagliardi@gwu.edu with any questions or concerns about accessibility & accommodations. 

 

NOTE: pre-sale is limited to 4 tickets per order.

 

Thank you for supporting Forbidden Planet Productions!

 

9 TO 5 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.mtishows.com

name: MAVAZI | 18th Annual Taste of Africa
description:
MAVAZI, meaning “clothing” in Swahili, is the 2026 edition of the African Student Association’s annual Taste of Africa showcase at The George Washington University. This year’s theme highlights the power of fashion as a form of cultural expression, storytelling, and identity across the African continent and diaspora.

Through a dynamic runway experience, MAVAZI brings together traditional and contemporary African fashion, showcasing the richness of textiles, beadwork, craftsmanship, and design. Each piece tells a story—reflecting history, heritage, and the evolving creativity of African designers and communities.

More than just a fashion show, MAVAZI is a celebration of culture, artistry, and unity. The event will feature curated looks, live performances, and an immersive atmosphere that honors the diversity and vibrancy of African cultures. Attendees can expect an evening that blends fashion, music, and storytelling into a powerful and memorable experience.

name: TEDxFoggyBottom Annual Conference 2025
description:
THIS IS A TICKETED EVENT. Head to https://www.tedxfoggybottom.org/ to purchase! 

What started in 2011 with a few students and a big idea has quickly become one of the largest student-organized TEDx events in the United States and around the world. Each year, TEDxFoggyBottom is brought to life by over 50 undergraduate students at The George Washington University in Washington, DC, who work to bring together some of the world's most incredible innovators, thinkers, and doers to inspire and collaborate with the Foggy Bottom community. We invite anyone in the DC community to join us for a day of learning, growing, and disruption. 

Tickets for the event include the ability to watch 8-10 TEDx Talks live from Betts Theater, connecting with local non-profits, a $100+ swag bag, a free catered lunch, and more.

This year's theme is First Gen Oasis; think of a classy beach party mixed with White Lotus and tropical, serene vibes. At this culminating event, we'll have dinner foods, themed mocktails, and live entertainment! We'll also award two first-gen students a $500 scholarship, reminisce on the experiences of our conference participants, and surprise you with theme-based activities throughout the evening. As always, our EBoard speakers and keynote speakers will inspire you as you get ready for graduation. 

Please RSVP to ensure we have the proper headcount for food. We can't wait to see you there!

Dress/attire ideas: like you're at a resort/on vacation, tropical prints, pastel colors, white linens/breezy fabrics, summer wedding guest, khakis, or anything that makes you feel comfortable and fabulous.

Hosted at Dacha Beer Garden in Shaw, Washington, DC, the event will feature a vibrant atmosphere, great food and drinks, and the opportunity to connect with fellow members of the GW community. Whether you’re celebrating milestones, honoring achievements, or simply enjoying time with friends, this formal is the perfect way to wrap up the year.

 

Dress to impress and get ready for an unforgettable evening with the GW Student Veterans community.

name: THE ART OF MATCHA: Green Tea  & Tea Ceremony Workshop
description:
🍵 Join us for a Matcha & Japanese Tea Ceremony Workshop! 🍵

Looking for a mid-afternoon escape from finals? Step into the world of Japanese tea with JCA! We’re hosting an immersive afternoon dedicated to the art, history, and flavors of green tea.

From refreshing cold-brewed Sencha to a formal tea ceremony performance, come learn about the journey of the leaf and the traditions behind the whisk.

What’s on the menu?
✨ Tastings of Sencha, Hojicha, and Gyokuro
✨ Traditional wagashi (sweet bean snacks)
✨ A live Tea Ceremony performance
✨ Complimentary Japanese tea bags to take home!

The Details:
📅 When: Friday, April 24th
⏰ Time: 2:30 PM – 4:00 PM
📍 Where: DH B114
👥 Note: Seats are limited to 15 participants, so register early!
🔗 Registration link (also in bio!): https://forms.gle/R1qTBKVMwfduJpmb9

Whether you’re a matcha addict or just curious about Japanese culture, we can’t wait to share a cup with you. See you there in our traditional Yukata and Hakama! 👘

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
location: USC Presentation Space (Across from Chaat House)
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: Red Alert - Self Defense Class
description:
an empowering, high-energy personal safety workshop designed specifically for sorority women. This program focuses on real-world situations college students may face, providing practical tools to increase confidence, awareness, and personal security on and off campus.

What Attendees Will Learn:

Situational Awareness on Campus & Social Events – Recognizing red flags, trusting intuition, and staying alert at parties, bars, and while walking at night.

Boundary Setting & Verbal Defense – How to confidently say “no,” project authority, and de-escalate uncomfortable situations.

Practical Self-Defense Techniques – Simple, effective physical skills designed for real-life scenarios — no experience needed.

Escape & Release Tactics – How to break free from common grabs and create space to get to safety.

Buddy System & Sister Safety Strategies – How to look out for one another and build a culture of awareness within the chapter.

This class is beginner-friendly, supportive, and judgment-free. It promotes strength, unity, and confidence

description:
George Hacks is a student-led organization that hosts a 48-hour innovation hackathon at GWU for the past 8 years. Our events bring together engineers, designers, policy thinkers, and builders to tackle real-world sustainability challenges.

This year, we are partnering with big names like the United Nations and AWS or our theme: Reboot the Earth. Participants will be challenged to rethink the systems that power our world, from food and climate infrastructure to healthcare, data accessibility, and resilient cities.

Register Here

The event culminates in live demos, final presentations, and sponsored prize tracks aligned with real-world sustainability and technology challenges. George Hacks isn’t just about building something in a weekend, it’s about launching ideas that can continue beyond it.

name: Simulation: Rising Tides
description:
Rising Tides is Strategic Crisis Simulations' fourth and final simulation of the academic year. Participants will navigate the challenges of military escalation and de-escalation in our annual U.S.-China relations sim.

It is 2028, and a collision between Chinese and Philippine vessels has prompted large-scale Chinese military exercises around Luzon Island and in the Taiwan Strait. Join Strategic Crisis Simulations for our signature annual U.S.—China simulation, Rising Tides. Participants have the option to play as suddenly surrounded Taiwanese officials, frustrated Chinese Ministry of State Security officers, interloping Vietnamese diplomats, or Philippine military officers reeling from a re-ignition of the dormant Mindanao conflict and a bruising presidential election.
 
Rising Tides will take place on Saturday, April 18th, 2026, from 11:00 AM EST to 5:00 PM EST. This simulation will be held in-person at George Washington University's Funger Hall, 2201 G St NW, Washington, DC 20052. We will be providing a catered lunch for attendees.
 
Prior sign-up is required to participate in Rising Tides. Sign up here!

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

In-person attendees will be provided food and drinks

name: AASA Spring GALA
description:
Join us for a gala celebrating the Asian American diaspora in the 2000’s through culture, community, dinner, speakers, performances, activities, and DANCING!!! ✨💝


⭐️Theme Details:

The 2000s embodied vibrancy, color, and a global explosion of expression that shaped our visual identity, cultural style, and the nostalgia we carry today. It marked a pivotal era in the emergence of “Asian American” as a widely recognized and evolving identity. Our connection to the 2000s is deepened by our growing voice in pop culture and by the fact that these were the years our parents spent raising us. 🫂💕 Yet in honoring these histories, GWU AASA takes on the responsibility of maintaining a critical lens. The same violence that underlaid the U.S. in the 2000s informs the escalations we witness two decades later. As we celebrate the struggles and resilience of Asian migrants and earlier generations of Asian Americans, we must not allow commodified nostalgia to obscure those violent processes. We remain committed—always—to our political line. 🫂💓✨

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
location: USC Presentation Space (Across from Chaat House)
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

description: This group is for both undergraduate and graduate school students who are nearing graduation and preparing for the next chapters in their lives. name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

name: "The Right Track" Film Screening and Panel Discussion
description:
The George Washington University Office of Advocacy and Support (OAS) and Rights4Girls invite you to a film screening of the groundbreaking documentary "The Right Track" onTuesday, March 31st, from 6:30pm-9:00pm in the Continental Ballroom of the University Student Center at located at 800 21st St NW, Washington, D.C.

 

Through the eyes of those who live it, "The Right Track" documentary spotlights the fight to end sex trafficking and human exploitation across North America. At its heart is the Survivor Model—a transformative approach that decriminalizes prostituted individuals while imposing strict penalties on pimps, traffickers, and sex buyers. Discover the courage it takes to escape “the life” on and off the track and the momentum needed to end sex trafficking for good. The Right Track is a must-watch for anyone invested in human dignity and justice. Click here to watch the trailer. 

 

After the film screening, please join us for a panel moderated by Carolina Bazan, Senior Program Manager at Rights4Girls. We will be joined by three incredible panelists: Peter Qualliotine, Melanie Thompson, and Cristian Eduardo. Click here to learn more about our panelists. 

 

GW's Office of Advocacy and Support (OAS) is a university office that provides trauma-informed and healing-centered confidential support to student survivors of intimate partner violence, sexual assault, and stalking. Click here to learn more about OAS.  

 

Rights4Girls advocates for the dignity and rights of young women and girls so that every girl can be safe and live a life free of violence and exploitation. Click here to learn more about Rights4Girls.

 

Join us for a film screening of "The Right Track" and panel discussion on Tuesday, March 31st, from 6:30pm-9:00pm in the Continental Ballroom of the University Student Center. Register below to grab your seat!

This program offers space for mindfulness, learning, and interfaith engagement while honoring Jain traditions of compassion, nonviolence, and spiritual reflection.

name: New Member Retreat
description:
Welcome to Fraternity and Sorority Life at GW! If you’ve recently joined a fraternity or sorority, the New Member Retreat is your next step—and it’s required.

This full-day experience is your opportunity to dive deeper into what it truly means to be part of the fraternity and sorority community. You’ll explore the national and local history of these organizations, understand the values that continue to shape Greek Life today, and have honest conversations about hazing prevention and outdated traditions that no longer reflect who we are.

Led by the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life, this retreat is also a chance to connect with new members from other chapters and councils, share your experiences, and start building a more inclusive, supportive community.

Check-in begins at 9:30 AM, and you must attend the full event to receive credit—so mark your calendar, bring your energy, and get ready to grow.

name: GW Students No Kings March

Join us as we march from campus to several federal buildings to make our voices heard, including the White House, the Department of Justice, the Education Department, and the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Headquarters.

Students are fired up—our futures are on the line, and we will stand to fight for our democracy.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

name: OneGW Summit: Community, Culture & Inclusion
description:
As we celebrate the 10th anniversary of the George Washington University hosting the Diversity Summit, we have the opportunity to boldly enter into the next decade of meaningful work - to truly be revolutionary. We are in a critical moment of our university's history and at the crux of building our institution’s future. In alignment with the Strategic Framework, and inspired by principles of community - derived from scholars, researchers, activists, changemakers, youth, and organizers - the 10th Diversity Summit will be named OneGW Summit: Community, Culture & Inclusion. With deep intention and purpose, we believe that centering the GW community in our work to amplify and celebrate diversity, collectively foster inclusion, and strive toward equity for all is how we move forward, together, as OneGW.

Remaining committed to our longstanding values, the OneGW Summit: Community, Culture & Inclusion will continue to be grounded in learning, dialogue, research, storytelling, and education on identity, social issues, diverse viewpoints, and sustainable positive action. The Summit will be:

A time of reflection, ideation, collaboration, and inspiration
An opportunity and curated experience for the whole GW community to bring all of their identities, lived experiences, stories, and various perspectives into a shared space
A groundswelling of engagement through civil discourse, deep listening, and healthy debate

It is our hope that the Summit is affirming to all and across all identities and viewpoints.

From celebrating milestones that helped us reach 10 years, to honoring members of the GW community making a significant impact in the world, and more, the Summit will serve as a catalyst for deeper engagement, connection, and meaningful dialogue across all differences. The Summit will honor the coexistence of multiple truths, demonstrating our strength to come together, break bread, and build as OneGW.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

location: Devine Theater -- Davis Arts Center -- Georgetown University
description:
It's last minute (today, Sunday!) but my colleague, Georgetown music Professor Ben Harbert, has co-written a play about "sound" in prison with two of his long-time DC-Jail collaborators.

The play explores the role of sound in prison through sound recordings, original music, and acting.  It’s an immersive look at a fundamental problem of incarceration today: prison is noisy, yet survival and sanity depend on learning to listen through the noise. 

All ticket proceeds go to Dr. Harbert's collaborators. Despite accomplishments that include starting a mentorship program in the DC Jail, being elected an Advisory Neighborhood Commissioner while incarcerated, publishing books, and building community organizations, they still face the barriers that too often follow people after incarceration.
 
I have five tickets (5).  Just send me an email (asdent@gwu.edu) or RSVP to this if you want to come.  I'll leave from Pete's in District House at 1:15. The play is 2-3. (You can also just meet me at the Devine Theater at 1:50)

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

While DC suffers from significant light pollution, the Unistellar telescope's unique software reduces the impact of the city lights on images of the night sky in real time, giving us a great view (weather permitting!) of planets, galaxies, nebulae and star clusters. On Tuesday, March 17 starting at 8:30pm, we will be observing various solar-system and deep sky objects such as Jupiter, the Orion Nebula and the Pleiades. Download the Unistellar app on your smartphone or tablet to follow along with our observations on your personal device. Feel free to drop by to observe for just a few minutes or stay for a while!

name: 46th Patricia Roberts Harris Banquet
description:
The George Washington University Law School BLSA invites you to attend the 46th Annual Patricia Roberts Harris Awards Banquet.

The George Washington University Law School Black Law Students Association (BLSA) is pleased to announce the 46th Annual Patricia Roberts Harris Awards Banquet, which will be held on March 28th, 2026, at the JW Marriott in Washington, D.C. Mrs. Harris, a distinguished alumna of The George Washington University National Law Center (now The George Washington University Law School), achieved remarkable milestones in her career. After graduating at the top of her class in 1960, she became a dedicated public servant, earning numerous accolades and pioneering many firsts. Among her many achievements, she was the first African-American woman to serve as a United States Ambassador, a member of the United States Cabinet, and as Dean of an American law school (Howard University School of Law).


In the spirit of her incredible achievements, this banquet serves as an occasion to honor and recognize BLSA’s outstanding graduating students, alumni, and sponsors, as well as the law school’s dedicated faculty and staff. Building strong, enduring relationships with legal organizations across the District of Columbia is central to ensuring that students have opportunities to follow in Mrs. Harris’ path. Therefore, BLSA extends an invitation for you to join us in this celebration of our distinguished alumna and exceptional community.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

name: International Oscars Film Screening: The Voice of Hind Rajab
description:
The Foreign Film Society, in collaboration with GW Students for Justice in Palestine, is proud to be hosting an exclusive screening of The Voice of Hind Rajab, a new film nominated for Best International Feature at this year's 2026 Oscars Ceremony. Based on real life events, the film tells the story of Hind Rajab, a five-year-old Palestinian victim of Israeli forces in Gaza in January 2024. Her story, as captured on emergency calls to Palestinian Red Crescent volunteers, has become one of the most haunting and widely reported accounts of the ongoing conflict. 

Don't miss this opportunity, as the film is still in theaters and yet to be released on streaming services!

This film screening is being organized by the GW Foreign Film Society and not by GW Students for Justice in Palestine (@sjpgwu).

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: Simulation: Caribbean Catastrophe
description:
Caribbean Catastrophe is Strategic Crisis Simulations' third simulation of the academic year and first of the Spring semester. Participants will be tasked with confronting the complex problems facing the region in the wake of the U.S. removal of Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro from power, especially as the U.S. now turns its eye to Cuba.

 

Tired of empty promises and an ever-worsening economy, the Cuban people have taken to the streets once again. Clashes have commenced across the island between internal security forces and the now unified opposition movement that has been emboldened by the recent removal of President Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela.
 
For the Cuban diaspora across the Americas, it's a moment they've waited for. For the international community, it's a crisis in the making. Players will navigate both domestic and foreign policy in "Caribbean Catastrophe" as the people of Cuba attempt to chart a new course. Participants will attempt to manage an entangled refugee crisis, address an ongoing viral epidemic in the region, and deal with the ever-unpredictable foreign policy of the United States that baffles both federal agencies and international organizations. Will outside observers intervene on behalf of the people, or prioritize their own security over calls for democracy and human rights?
 
Caribbean Catastrophe will take place on Saturday, February 21st, 2026, from 11:00 AM EST to 5:00 PM EST. This simulation will be held in-person at George Washington University's Funger Hall, 2201 G St NW, Washington, DC 20052. We will be providing a catered lunch for attendees.
 
Prior sign-up is required to participate in Caribbean Catastrophe. Sign up here!

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: Impact of the Belt and Road Initiative in Africa
description:
Event Overview

The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has had a monumental impact on Sino African relations over the past few years. We at Operation US Africa are bringing experts in Africa, China, and the United States to discuss the economic ramifications of this project including infrastructure construction, investment, and critical minerals. Social impacts including the change in diplomatic perception of China compared to the United States in Africa.

10:30am - 11:00am Check in, Breakfast provided

11am - 12pm: High Level Dialogue: US-Africa ties in the context of the BRI in Africa

The United States has had consistent bipartisan interest in the construction of economic infrastructure such as the Lobito Corridor to receive critical minerals to counter Chinese influence as well as prior diplomatic efforts to secure Kenya as a diplomatic partner. This conversation comes at a critical moment in US-African relations where the US can change its position to a country focused on economic development in Africa rather than just aid. We seek to foster professional discussion and bipartisan agreement on actions the US should take to collaborate with nations as partners. This panel will examine the American and African perspective on the BRI and how the US position on the continent has changed since its introduction in 2014.

H.E. Frank Tayali, Minister of Transport and Logistics, Republic of Zambia (virtual, if confirmed)

TBD African Affairs at Dept. of State

Ambassador (ret) Troy Fitrell, fmr. US Ambassador to the Republic of Guinea, Board Member, SAGINT (confirmed speaker)

Moderator: Mr. Julian Pecquet, US Correspondent at the Africa Report (confirmed moderator)

12pm-12:30pm Lunch Break

12:30-1:30pm: Economic Impact of the Belt and Road Initiative in Africa

From military exercises in South Africa, to construction of ports in Ghana to railways in Kenya, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has made a substantial imprint on the Africa continent. This panel will evaluate the Economic impact of the project on countries across the continent whether through improving economic trade axes such as bridges, roads, and railways, increasing the exploitation of rare earth minerals, the BRI has changed interpretations of the sphere of African investment to make infrastructure construction more feasible. Furthermore, the emerging market for Chinese goods such as electric vehicles, cellphones, and t-shirts sold at lower cost than their Western counterparts have flooded African markets. This panel will explore the Economic Impact of the Belt and Road Initiative and corresponding Chinese influence in Africa.

Mr. Andrew Dabalen, Africa Chief Economist, World Bank (confirmed speaker)

Ebenezer Obadare, Douglas Dillon Senior Fellow for Africa Studies, Council on Foreign Relations (confirmed speaker)

Bright Simons, Founder and President, mPedigree (confirmed virtual speaker)

Moderator: Professor David Shinn, Former US Ambassador to Burkina Faso and Ethiopia (confirmed moderator)
 

1:35pm-2:35pm: Social Impact of the Belt and Road Initiative in Africa

The Belt and Road Initiative with its infrastructure endeavors has a social subsection focused on promoting China in African media and in the social consciousness. This panel will discuss exactly how much the Chinese efforts at improving infrastructure and engaging African elites impact how Africans view China in the context of great power competition with the United States and its overall reliability as a diplomatic partner.

TBD Kenya

Associate Professor at Georgetown University, Ken Opalo (confirmed virtual speaker)

Professor Paul Kepp, Former Assistant Director of CIA, Chief of Ops Africa, Professor at The Institute of World Politics (confirmed speaker)

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

name: Alexei Navalny Memorial Vigil: Two Years of Remembrance
description:
Join the GW Russian-speaking community and allies as we commemorate the second anniversary of Alexei Navalny's death in Russian prison.

Who was Alexei Navalny?
Alexei Navalny (1976-2024) was Russia's most prominent opposition leader and anti-corruption activist. After surviving a poisoning attempt in 2020, he courageously returned to Russia knowing he would be imprisoned. On February 16, 2024, he was killed in a remote Arctic prison colony by Putin's regime.

Why This Matters:
Navalny's courage inspired millions worldwide to stand against authoritarianism and corruption. His final message was clear: "Don't give up." This vigil honors his legacy and demonstrates solidarity with those fighting for democracy and human rights in Russia and beyond.

Event Details:

Date: Sunday, February 16, 2026

Time: 12:00 PM

Location: Boris Nemtsov Plaza (2698-2600 Wisconsin Ave NW, Washington, DC 20007)

What to Bring: Optional - flowers, candles, signs

All GW students, faculty, and community members are welcome. No prior knowledge required.

"The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good people to do nothing."

description:
The GW and local D.C., Maryland and Virginia communities are invited to join the Walk for Peace on the final stop of their monumental journey. A special program featuring a message of peace, blessings, and meditation will be held on Wednesday, Feb. 11, at the Charles E. Smith Center.

 

This inspiring movement began on Oct. 26, 2025, when nearly two dozen Buddhist monks (also referred to as Bhantes) and Aloka the Peace Dog, from the Huong Dao Vipassana Bhavana Center in Fort Worth, Texas, embarked on a 2,300-mile walking journey to Washington, D.C., to promote national healing, unity, and compassion. 

 

Media interested in attending must provide valid media credentials and email gwmedia@gwu.edu to register. 

 

Additional Information

Please note the following:

 

Event details are tentative and subject to change without notice to registrants.
This event is open to the general public.
Tickets are not required but seats are first-come-first-served.
The Smith Center has a strict no-bag policy. No bags or other personal items will be permitted into the Smith Center for the program.

Drawing on the work of bell hooks, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., and Valarie Kaur, we will examine how love has been used as a transformative tool in movements for justice, liberation, and social change.

This event is open to all and offers a space to learn, share knowledge, and challenge ourselves in community. Enjoy free food, participate in a charm bracelet–making activity, and engage in meaningful dialogue with others. Come curious, come hungry, and come ready to connect and reflect.

Please be advised that this event has reached capacity. We encourage you to attend a public event for the Walk for Peace on Feb. 11. For more information, visit our webpage.

GW community members are invited to attend a special program featuring the Walk for Peace on Tuesday, Feb. 10, in Betts Theatre. A limited number of tickets are open to only GW students, faculty and staff. Advanced registration is required. This event is closed to media. 

 

This inspiring movement began on Oct. 26, 2025, when nearly two dozen Buddhist monks (also referred to as Bhantes) and Aloka the Peace Dog, from the Huong Dao Vipassana Bhavana Center in Fort Worth, Texas, embarked on a 2,300-mile walking journey to Washington, D.C., to promote national healing, unity, and compassion. 

 

Be part of this global event while experiencing the powerful message of peace that this movement represents.

 

Additional Information

Please note the following:

 

Event details are tentative and subject to change without notice to registrants.
Tickets are limited and first-come-first-served. Advanced registration on Engage is required.
No bags or other personal items will be permitted into Betts Theatre for the program.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: Spring 2026 Weekly Poker Session (Week 4)
description:
ome and join the Poker Club for our Fall 2026 weekly sessions! Table play occurs every Friday. Anyone interested at any skill level is encouraged to join.

 

The rule structure is Texas no limit hold'em. Everyone will receive a fictional cash bankroll upon registration ($13,500), and that money stays with you throughout the semester. Each session players are allowed to "buy-in" three times if they bankrupt then they will have to come back next session to play again. Any profits and losses incurred during weekly play will accumulate, and players are ranked based on their bankroll value for end-of-semester tournament qualification. The tournament rounds will take place during the last two Fridays of the semester before finals.

 

We hope to see you soon, and please reach out to gwupokerclub@gmail.com or @gwupoker on Instagram with any questions. Also please join the groupme (groupme.com/join_group/110245251/rajw6Dbf).

location: DUQUES HALL, 2201 G St NW, Washington, DC 20052
description:
Join Next Generation Impact (NGI) and the GWU Impact Investment Hub for NGI’s official launch event on February 6 from 2:00–3:30 PM. This panel discussion will bring together leaders from policy, finance, and impact-focused industries to explore how greater cross-sector collaboration can strengthen an impact investing industry that is currently underperforming in both impact and returns.

Panelists will discuss what needs to change in impact investing, what is working and should be scaled, and where stronger collaboration is needed to break down silos and bridge financing gaps in the development space. The event will also feature student poster presentations and opportunities to learn about research and internship pathways with the Impact Investment Hub.

Open to GWU students, recent graduates, and DC-area professionals interested in impact investing, economics, and international development

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

ome and join the Poker Club for our Fall 2026 weekly sessions! Table play occurs every Friday. Anyone interested at any skill level is encouraged to join.

The tournament rounds will take place during the last two Fridays of the semester before finals.

 

We hope to see you soon, and please reach out to gwupokerclub@gmail.com or @gwupoker on Instagram with any questions. Also please join the groupme (groupme.com/join_group/110245251/rajw6Dbf).

Join us at Buff & Brew for light snacks and to hear from Ishita Borikar, MVC resident and artist! Her collection of works blends realism with expressive ink and illustrative styles. Her realistic portraits focus on capturing emotion, personality, and subtle human details, while her ink pieces explore movement, contrast, and storytelling.

Much of her work is inspired by cartoons, anime, and Desi culture, drawing from bold linework, exaggerated expression, and cultural symbolism. By combining traditional realism with stylized influences, she aims to bridge different visual languages and reflect the way identity, nostalgia, and pop culture intersect.

name: Trip to Visit the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum
description:
Every year around 27 January, UNESCO pays tribute to the memory of the victims of the Holocaust and reaffirms its unwavering commitment to counter antisemitism, racism, and other forms of intolerance that may lead to group-targeted violence. The date marks the anniversary of the liberation of the Auschwitz Birkenau German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp by Soviet troops on 27 January 1945.

It was officially proclaimed, in November 2005, International Day of Commemoration in Memory of the Victims of the Holocaust by the United Nations General Assembly.

In commemoration of International Holocaust Remembrance Day 2026 we will be hosting a trip to The US Holocaust Memorial Museum (snow permitting) THIS FRIDAY (1/30). 



United States Holocaust Memorial Museum Visit

Join Us for a Museum Trip!

About Scott Wayne

Scott Wayne is an international development consultant with over 25 years of experience focused on sustainable destination development. His work centers on applying the UN Sustainable Development Goals to infrastructure projects, public–private partnerships, tourism development, economic and environmental impact assessments, policy development, and strategic planning for inclusive and sustainable growth.

He has worked with a wide range of clients, including the Asian Development Bank, World Bank, World Trade Organization, USAID, private-sector organizations, governments, and NGOs in more than 60 countries worldwide.

Scott is also an accomplished author, having written several travel guides for Lonely Planet on Egypt, Sudan, and Mexico, as well as a book on North Africa for Sierra Club Books.

Dress code: business casual

If you missed info session 1 (or just want to see us again), this is another opportunity to learn more about our organization. You must attend at least 1 info session to be considered for membership. 

The Eta Chapter of Delta Phi Epsilon is a co-ed foreign service society with a 97-year tradition of developing competent, creative, and ethical leaders for the world. Founded in 1929 to encourage fellowship, excellence, and professional development among those studying or engaged with international affairs and foreign service, the Eta Chapter continues to uphold this prestigious tradition.

DPE’s Eta Chapter actively seeks out the best and brightest students at The George Washington University. Regardless of major, students in good standing with the University who demonstrate exceptional academic and professional capability, an enthusiasm for international relations, a commitment to public service, and strong personal character are offered a place in our induction process. Alumni of Eta Chapter have gone on to become influential members of the American diplomatic corps, the defense community, international legal and business establishments, non-profits, and Congress. Fill out our interest form here.

name: GW SAS Charity Gala
description:
Our 2025 Charity Gala  will be one of the biggest SAS events of the year in order to fundraise for Ashiyanaa and promote their mission. It would be an elegant night with appetizers, an open bar, and an engaging program to bring folks from GW and beyond together for an important cause. Additionally, we will be inviting GW SAS alumni to our event for an opportunity to network and reflect upon their memorable time at GW. This gala would be the first of many initiatives to build a GW SAS alumni network to ensure that the SAS community lasts beyond our years as undergraduates. It would signal a long-lasting commitment to civic engagement and empowerment, turning SAS’s cultural pride into a legacy of tangible action.

The GW South Asian Society, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, has partnered with the charity Ashiyanaa for the 2025-2026 school year. Ashiyanaa, a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization, provides culturally-competent support services to South Asian women and children impacted by interpersonal violence. Over the years, their services and programs have expanded and currently serve all South Asians with origins in Afghanistan, Bhutan, Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. They utilize extensive community outreach to lead programs that address the ongoing needs of South Asians in the Washington, D.C. metro area and beyond. By centering a charity that prioritizes culturally competent care, we aim to challenge the stigma around gender-based violence and encourage open dialogue around healing and accountability within our community.

name: Hazing Education and Prevention Spring Extension
description:
As a member of GW’s fraternity and sorority community, it’s on all of us to create a culture of safety, respect, and accountability. That’s why Hazing Education and Prevention Spring Extension is mandatory for all current and new members of fraternities and sororities at GW.

Hosted by the Office of Student Life, you'll dive into what hazing looks like, how to recognize and prevent it, and how to build a chapter culture that supports true brotherhood and sisterhood.

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
location: Multicultural Student Services Center - MSSC (Multipurpose Programming Room) USC 5th Floor
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

The Annual FSK 24/7 Finals Snack & Slime Bar is officially opening on December 13th at 6:00 p.m. in the FSK 8th Floor Lounge, and this year we’re going all out. Need fuel for late-night studying? We’ve got snacks, coffee, hot cocoa, and tea flowing around the clock to keep you going. The bar will stay open until December 18th (or until supplies run out), so stop by anytime and grab what you need to power through!

But wait… you know FSK, we always have something extra up our sleeve. This semester, we’re adding pop-up surprises to celebrate the Snack Bar opening!

Saturday: Pop-Up Pancake Night
Monday: Pop-Up Hot Chocolate Night

You truly never know what to expect with the FSK Snack Bar, and that’s the fun of it!

And of course, the TikTok-inspired Slime Station is back! Swing by the 8th Floor Lounge to take a study break, make your own slime, shake off the stress, and tap into your creativity.

Let’s conquer finals together, one snack, one slime, and one surprise pop-up at a time!

name: Whose Campus? Collective strategy on student power and the Popular University!
description:
Join GWU SAI on December 11th at 4:30 PM in the MSSC (USC 5th Floor) for an end-of-year collective strategy session on building power to win the university we want to see: A Popular University.

A Popular University is a democratic university, built by and for the people in service of liberation. It is a university where students and workers have decision making power—not the Board of Trustees, administration, or government who continue to prioritize profit-making while we bear the costs. As attacks on students and workers escalate, It’s time for us to strategize and defend our community. We hope to see you there!

name: Spiritual Bites & Interfaith Insights
description:
Join us for an exciting bi-weekly dialogue series where the GW community explores how our religious, spiritual, and secular beliefs shape our personal values, relationships, and worldviews. We’ll discuss how practices such as meditation and prayer offer strength during challenging times, promote peace, and encourage well-being. Conversations will also touch on interfaith respect, cooperation, the ethics of service and compassion, and navigating the intersection of religion, politics, and social justice. A wide range of topics will be explored, including interfaith dating and family dynamics. This is a journey of thought-provoking discussions, and we hope you’ll join us!

 

Be sure to bring your lunch, or use your Meal Plan (Swipe, Dining Dollar, Debit/Credit, and Cash) so we can all eat together in community.

name: Simulation: Triangular Troubles
description:
Strategic Crisis Simulations is hosting its second simulation of the academic year on Saturday, December 6th. Triangular Troubles, is about efforts to combat transnational crime in Southeast Asia’s Golden Triangle.

 

A shocking report from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime has ripped the veil off a sprawling transnational criminal network in the Golden Triangle. Evidence has linked a number of officials, militias, and private enterprises in an enormous drug and money-laundering scheme. Recent raids on suspected sites have exploded into lethal clashes along the border. name: Statistics Graduate Student Seminar 2025 Dec 5th
description:
We are delighted to announce that this week's seminar will be given by  Navid Nezamabadi . 
 
Date & Time: 12.5th (this Friday), 3-4pm

Location: Rome hall conference room 771
 
Speaker: Navid Nezamabadi (GWU Statistics)

Title:  Intermittent Demand Forecasting for Spare Part Inventory Control Problems
  
Abstract: Inventory control problems are an ever-expanding realm of logistical dilemmas that have been thoroughly explored in the last 50 years. A general overview of the field will be given, touching on typical problems such as the newsvendor, base-stock, (Q, R), and (s, S) problems. A deeper dive will be presented on spare part problems and common methods used to address their specific difficulties. Being characterized by intermittent demand (many zero demand counts), many traditional inventory control methods perform poorly on spare part data. Compound Poisson, Poisson-Gamma, and a non-parametric Bayesian approach shall be presented, accompanied by a novel zero-inflated Poisson-Gamma method that builds on previous research. Applications of these methods will be touched on, and their collective contribution to the industry appraised.
 
Attendance of Phd&Msc students is strongly encouraged. Hope to see some of you there!

name: Fall 2025 Weekly Poker Session (Week 11)
description:
Come and join the Poker Club for our Fall 2024 weekly sessions! Table play occurs every Friday. Anyone interested at any skill level is encouraged to join.

 

The rule structure is Texas no limit hold'em. Everyone will receive a fictional cash bankroll upon registration ($13,500), and that money stays with you throughout the semester. Each session players are allowed to "buy-in" three times if they bankrupt then they will have to come back next session to play again. Any profits and losses incurred during weekly play will accumulate, and players are ranked based on their bankroll value for end-of-semester tournament qualification. The tournament rounds will take place during the last two Fridays of the semester before finals.

 

We hope to see you soon, and please reach out to gwupokerclub@gmail.com or @gwupoker on Instagram with any questions. Also please join the groupme (groupme.com/join_group/110245251/rajw6Dbf).

name: Movie Night in Alexandria: Predator - Badlands @AMC Courthouse Plaza 8
description:
First Hunt.

LAST CHANCE. 

“Predator: Badlands,” which stars Elle Fanning and Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi, is set in the future on a remote planet, where a young Predator (Schuster-Koloamatangi), outcast from his clan, finds an unlikely ally in Thia (Fanning) and embarks on a treacherous journey in search of the ultimate adversary. The film is directed by Dan Trachtenberg and produced by John Davis, Dan Trachtenberg, Marc Toberoff, Ben Rosenblatt, Brent O’Connor.

The story is set in the future on a remote, deadly planet called Genna and centers on a young Predator (Yautja) named Dek (Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi), who is an outcast from his clan for being considered a "runt" and not aggressive enough. Determined to prove his worth, he embarks on a dangerous quest to hunt an "un-killable" apex creature. 
 
During his journey, Dek forms an unlikely alliance with Thia (Elle Fanning), a damaged synthetic (android) from the nefarious Weyland-Yutani Corporation. Thia has her own mission to find her "sister," Tessa (also played by Elle Fanning), another synthetic who has a more cold-blooded approach and serves the corporation's aggressive AI, MU/TH/UR. 
 
The film explores themes of teamwork, found family, and challenging traditional, violent ideologies, as Dek and Thia (along with a small alien sidekick named Bud) must work together to survive the planet's hostile environment and confront the corporation's forces.
 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=43R9l7EkJwE

Will be meeting in the lobby Guthridge Hall @7pm.

description:
Forbidden Planet Productions presents... Alice by Heart, directed by Emily Saffer! 

Curiouser and curiouser! 🦩📚 Alice By Heart, written by Steven Slater and Duncan Sheik, is a twist on Lewis Caroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Set in the rubble of World War II London, Alice by Heart reimagines Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland as a journey of grief, love, and the power of imagination. When the world above is crumbling, Alice escapes into her beloved book to find comfort and courage—discovering that sometimes the only way to heal is through the stories we hold in our hearts. 🩵 Join us Down the Hole in Wonderland! 🐇📖

name: Writing Letters to Political Prisoners and Repressed in Russia.
description:
Hello,

The Russian Speaking Association at GW invites you to take part in a meaningful event — Letters to the Repressed in Russia.

We’ll be writing to people unjustly imprisoned in Russia on politically motivated charges — Russians, Ukrainians, Americans, Europeans, and others — silenced for their political opinions or opposition to the war.

Your words can make a difference. A single letter can protect someone from torture, lift their spirits, and remind them they are not forgotten.

We’ll translate your letters into Russian and send them online through the official prison system. You may remain anonymous and can choose to write by hand or digitally — just upload your letter to a shared Google Doc at the end.

📅 Friday, November 14 | 5–7 PM
📍 University Student Center, Room 310 (800 21st St NW, Washington, DC 20052)

Learn more and find helpful resources here: https://linktr.ee/rsagw

We hope to see you there.
— Russian Speaking Association at GW 🪆

Community

Join the Sikh Student Association (SSA) for Langar, a traditional Sikh community meal that embodies the values of equality, service (seva), and humility. Held in Kogan Plaza, this event invites all students, faculty, and staff to enjoy a free vegetarian meal served by SSA members in the true spirit of inclusivity. Rooted in the centuries-old Sikh practice of sharing food and fellowship, Langar welcomes everyone—regardless of faith, background, or status—to sit together and share a meal as equals. Throughout the event, SSA members will share the meaning and history behind Langar, fostering conversation about community, compassion, and the importance of serving others. Participants will leave not only nourished but also inspired by the Sikh values of unity, generosity, and social harmony.

name: Bhangra Panel
description:
Bhangra Panel

 

Hosted by: GW Bhangra 

 

November 8, 2025 

 

7 pm 

 

Educational/Community 

 

Continental Ballroom 

 

Bhangra Beyond the Beat invites the GW community to experience the vibrant energy, history, and cultural significance of Bhangra, a Punjabi folk dance that originated in Northern India. Through storytelling, visuals, and music, the event will explore how Bhangra has evolved from its traditional roots into a global expression of identity, joy, and unity—welcoming people of all cultures, faiths, and backgrounds. Following a brief presentation, participants can join an interactive workshop featuring a live DJ and Dhol player, learning basic dance steps and the meaning behind the props used in performance. With snacks, stories, and shared celebration, this event embodies the spirit of Interfaith Week by showing how Bhangra transcends difference and brings communities together through rhythm, movement, and connection.

name: New Member Retreat
description:
Welcome to Fraternity and Sorority Life at GW! If you’ve recently joined a fraternity or sorority, the New Member Retreat is your next step—and it’s required.

This full-day experience is your opportunity to dive deeper into what it truly means to be part of the fraternity and sorority community. You’ll explore the national and local history of these organizations, understand the values that continue to shape Greek Life today, and have honest conversations about hazing prevention and outdated traditions that no longer reflect who we are.

Led by the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life, this retreat is also a chance to connect with new members from other chapters and councils, share your experiences, and start building a more inclusive, supportive community.

Check-in begins at 9:00 AM, and you must attend the full event to receive credit—so mark your calendar, bring your energy, and get ready to grow.

Featuring guest speakers, each will highlight a different Prophet—such as Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad (peace be upon them)—offering insights into their lives, messages, and enduring relevance today. Each session includes a 30-minute talk followed by a 15-minute Q&A, allowing for reflection and discussion. Participants will gain a deeper appreciation of Islam’s Prophetic tradition and its emphasis on faith, compassion, and moral guidance. Open to all, this event offers an enriching opportunity for both Muslims and non-Muslims to engage with familiar figures through a new spiritual and cultural lens, deepening understanding across faiths.

During this session, participants will be guided through gentle meditation and deep rest accompanied by the soothing sounds of singing bowls, chimes, and other harmonic instruments. The combination of sound healing and Yoga Nidra—a form of guided meditation often called “yogic sleep”—invites the body to release tension while the mind enters a state of calm awareness. Open to all members of the GW community, this peaceful practice offers an opportunity to pause, reconnect, and restore your energy at the end of a meaningful week of interfaith reflection and connection.

Educational
