Join two GW faculty members—an Iranian-born Muslim and an American-born Jew—for an engaging and heartfelt interfaith workshop exploring how faith, culture, and identity shape our relationships and shared commitments. Drawing on years of dialogue and partnership at GW and beyond, the facilitators will open with personal stories of learning, solidarity, and friendship across differences. Participants will then engage in small-group and whole-group conversations reflecting on values such as justice, compassion, and resilience, culminating in a collaborative activity to identify practical ways to strengthen interfaith and intercultural understanding on campus. This interactive session invites all to listen deeply, share authentically, and build a community rooted in empathy and mutual respect.

name: Museum Resume Workshop Series: Session 2: Resumes and Cover Letters
location: The GW Museum and The Textile Museum
description:
Join The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum for part two of our four-part professional development workshop series for students interested in a career in museums, the arts, or other cultural institutions. Each session of the workshop will focus on improving one aspect of your application materials to give you the best chances of landing an interview for your next job. The series will conclude with a resume review with department heads from The GW Museum and The Textile Museum.

In this session, you’ll have the opportunity to think about your resume and your cover letter as tools to land you an interview. Led by museum director John Wetenhall, the workshop will guide you through how to effectively convey yourself in a resume and a cover letter-- and what should be included in each.

The museum will provide light snacks and drinks during the workshop. This series is open to all GW students, so use this opportunity to meet peers with similar interests across programs such as museum studies, museum education, anthropology, archeology, history, religion studies, and more!

November 6, 2025 

 

4 pm 

 

Dialogue 

 

Amphitheater

 

Abrahamic Conversation invites the GW community to a thought-provoking interfaith dialogue among an Imam, a Priest, and a Rabbi exploring life’s deepest questions: What happens to the soul after death? How does each faith understand the afterlife? And how do these traditions relate to one another in matters of spirit and destiny? This moderated panel, followed by an open Q&A, creates space for curiosity, learning, and meaningful exchange. Drawing on sacred texts, theology, and lived experience, the conversation will illuminate both the distinct insights and shared hopes within Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Participants will leave with a richer understanding of the soul and a renewed appreciation for the power of interfaith dialogue to foster empathy and connection.

Many Faiths, Many Flavors: Israel is an immersive cultural showcase celebrating the rich tapestry of Israel’s religious and cultural communities—Jewish, Muslim, Christian, Druze, Bedouin, Ethiopian, Russian, Mizrahi, and more. Through tasting stations, music, storytelling, and interactive activities, participants will experience how these diverse traditions intertwine in everyday life. Each station will feature a bite-sized snack paired with history, symbols, and teachings from that community. The event also includes a Kahoot trivia game, soundscapes, and a collaborative “Community Mosaic” highlighting shared values. A short video and reflection space will invite deeper dialogue about unity in diversity. Participants will leave with a fuller appreciation of interfaith coexistence and the beauty of cultures woven together.

Rest as Resistance: An Interfaith Practice of Renewal invites the GW community to pause, breathe, and embrace rest as a sacred, life-giving act. Inspired by Tricia Hersey’s Rest is Resistance: A Manifesto and the work of The Nap Ministry, this interactive workshop explores rest as both a spiritual practice and a form of resistance to a culture of constant productivity. Through reflection, breathwork, and storytelling, participants will engage wisdom from diverse faith and cultural traditions that honor rest as holy—whether through Sabbath, meditation, prayer, or silence. Together, we’ll cultivate rituals of renewal and collective care, leaving with a deeper sense of belonging and the reminder that rest is not a retreat from the world, but a sacred way of returning to it, whole and well.

description:

November 3, 2025

 

12 pm

Gelman Library, 7th Floor Room 713 


Explore the rich history of global faith traditions at a drop-in tabletop exhibit in Gelman Library’s Kiev Judaica Collection, featuring the complete first English edition of The Religious Ceremonies and Customs of the Several Nations of the Known World (1731–1739) by Bernard Picart and Jean-Frédéric Bernard. This six-volume masterpiece, renowned as an early work of comparative religious study, depicts the rituals and beliefs of Jews, Muslims, Hindus, Native Americans, Catholics, and Protestants through detailed engravings and descriptive texts. Visitors are invited to reflect on the work’s humanizing approach to diverse traditions, learn about its historical context, and discover Gelman Library’s rare book collections and resources for exploring the world’s spiritual heritage. name: Statistics Graduate Student Seminar 2025 Oct 31th
description:
Dear Statistics/Biostatistics graduate students,

 
We are delighted to announce that this week's seminar will be given by Prof. Reza Modarres. 
 
Date & Time: 10.31th (this Friday), 3-4pm

Location: Philips hall room 110

Speaker: Professor Reza Modarres (GWU Statistics)

Title:  High Dimensional Data Analysis - A Proximity Based Approach
  
Abstract: High-dimensional data, where the number of features p far exceeds the number of observations n, has become increasingly prevalent in modern science and technology. From microarrays and fMRI to network traffic analysis, researchers are confronted with datasets consisting of millions of variables measured on only a few dozen samples.

Classical multivariate methods, which assume n ≫ p, can lose effectiveness or even fail entirely when dealing with high-dimensional, low-sample-size (HDLSS) settings. In this context, interpoint distances play a crucial role, providing a way to reduce complex multivariate relationships into simpler one-dimensional summaries. By focusing on distances and dissimilarities, we avoid reliance on distributional assumptions and use the concentration of measure phenomenon to our advantage.

We explore two high-dimensional dissimilarity measures and their convergence as p → ∞. Using these measures, we introduce new statistics for testing the equality of high-dimensional distributions, and we propose novel methods for classification, clustering, and change-point detection. Distance matrices serve as key representations in settings where direct access to data is impractical, or the data is inherently relational, such as in social networks or transportation systems.

We investigate the connection between the eigenstructure of distance matrices and the presence of outliers. Furthermore, we establish an equivalence between constant distance matrices and distributional equality, and present tests for determining whether a distance matrix exhibits constant structure. We also study the eigenvalues of k distance matrices for testing distributional equality and further explore the spectral properties of dissimilarity matrices under HDLSS conditions.

Attendance of Phd&Msc students is strongly encouraged. Hope to see some of you there!

name: Coffee with Alumni | Chris Wimbush CCAS '09 | Interim President, Catholics for Choice
description:
Chris Wimbush became the Interim President of Catholics for Choice on September 1, 2024, after serving as Chief Operating Officer. In this role, he has navigated significant global and political changes, including Donald Trump's reelection and the transition in the papacy. Chris emphasizes strategic planning, operational sustainability, and expanding the organization's impact.

After completing law school, Chris gained experience as a law clerk for U.S. District Court Judge Raymond A. Jackson in the Eastern District of Virginia. He then transitioned to work as a litigator at a prominent law firm in Washington, D.C. In addition, he has worked as a consultant in public sector management, held senior positions in human resources and operations, and served in executive roles focusing on cultural and operational transformation within professional services firms, startups, and nonprofits over the past decade.

Chris holds a Master of Business Administration from Babson College, a JD from the University of Virginia School of Law, and a BA in political science with a focus on public policy from George Washington University.

name: Nashman Center 15th Anniversary
description:
Join us as we celebrate 15 years of the Nashman Center for Civic Engagement and Public Service—a milestone honoring our history, impact, and community.

This fall, the George Washington University community will gather to honor 15 years of the Nashman Center—a milestone celebration of civic engagement, public service, and community impact that has shaped generations of GW students and strengthened our partnerships across Washington, D.C. and beyond.

Since its founding in 2009-10, GW's Center for Civic Engagement and Public Service has been a hub where students, faculty, staff, alumni, and community members come together to learn, serve, and lead. Renamed in 2015 to honor Associate Professor Emerita Honey W. Nashman, a pioneer of community service and social justice at GW, the Center has carried forward her vision of higher education as a force for equity and civic responsibility.

On October 25, 2025 we’ll reflect on our legacy, spotlight stories from students and alumni, and celebrate the people and partnerships that make civic engagement central to the GW experience.

description:

Goose will demonstrate some of the essential tasks service dogs can perform, offering real-world insight into how these partnerships empower individuals with chronic conditions. 

The evening will conclude with a Q & A providing space for open dialogue and education around chronic illness and service animals.

name: International Economic Development in Africa
description:
Join us for our signature event this fall. Meet with high level ambassadors and economists to discuss International Economic Development in Africa including Mr. Richard Cambridge, Advisor to Diaspora Vice President at the World Bank, H.E. Chibamba, Zambian Ambassador to the United States, and Mr. Jonah Mushayi, Minister Counsellor for Trade and Investment at the Zimbabwean Embassy to the United States.

We will be discussing the ever changing sphere of International Economic Development in Africa and how African countries can maintain autonomy, providing meaningful progress to their populations in this era of great power competition. We also will focus on how African countries can activate diaspora populations to improve economic conditions at home. Caribbean food will be served.

name: Simulation: Metallic Momentum
description:
Strategic Crisis Simulations is hosting its first major simulation of the academic year on Saturday, October 18th. Metallic Momentum is a simulation about conflicts over influence and local control, as well as impacts of mining, in South America's "Lithium Triangle."

 

Approximately half of the world’s lithium can be found in the "Lithium Triangle" in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile. As the world’s demand for the metal soars, nations and corporations alike set their sights on the region.

Bolivia’s new government begins to exploit its untapped potential through foreign investment and economic reform as it faces an economic crisis. Chile, the region’s dominant producer, grapples with internal conflict over the role of state and private firms. Meanwhile, Argentina is undergoing rapid expansion of the sector, fueled by government support and foreign capital.

Great opportunity comes with great risks: land rights disputes, water contamination, and battles over privatization will shake host governments.

In the Lithium Triangle, multinational corporations, great powers, and regional governments are intent on taking their place in the sun, and no one will escape the whirlwind.

 

Sign up for Metallic Momentum at the link below:

https://forms.gle/TxgC4yZLH8JahB7m9

name: Statistics Graduate Student Seminar 2025 Oct 17th
description:
We are delighted to announce that this week's seminar will be given by Zexin Ren. This work focuses on synthetic data methods for survival endpoints. 
 
Date & Time: 10.17th (this Friday), 3-4pm

Location: Rome Hall 204

Speaker: Zexin Ren (3rd year Phd candidate)

Title:  SynthIPD: assumption-lean synthetic individual patient data generation
  
Abstract: Individual patient data (IPD) are essential for statistical analysis in clinical research, yet access is often limited due to privacy concerns, high data-sharing costs, and proprietary restrictions. Conventional approaches to synthetic data generation, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), require a large piece of IPD as training set. This paper introduces an assumption-lean, three-step methodology for generating synthetic IPD with survival endpoints, requiring no IPD for training. In a nutshell, it digitizes the reported Kaplan-Meier(KM) plots and generates covariates that match the reconstructed data. Compared with existing IPD reconstruction methods, our approach is the first to exploit Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) for high-accuracy digitization, and the first to provide covariate information. We demonstrate the method’s potential through two detailed case studies and complementary simulation studies.
 
Attendance of Phd&Msc students is strongly encouraged. Hope to see some of you there!

name: Night of Light
description: Night of Light is a community event and opportunity for young Muslims to convene and listen to the recitation of the Qur’an in Arabic and reflect on its translation with licensed Muslim scholars and reciters. The objective of this event is to strengthen the connection of attendees to the Quran and see it as a source of light and comfort, and a text to be actively engaged with and reflected upon. The program will begin with an introduction to the chapter being recited and reciters taking turns reciting sections of a Quranic chapter. After each recitation, a licensed Quranic teacher and scholar will share reflections and teachings from the recited section. This process will repeat until the chapter’s recitation is finished, after which the program will end.

name: Hack Your Ramen: From Packet to Perfect -- Thursday, October 9th -- 6:30PM -- Free Dinner!!
description:
Hack Your Ramen — From Packet to Perfect (10 spots only!)

It’s late. You’re stressed. You’re spending too much at Western Market.

RAMEN.

It’s fast, it’s cheap — but let’s face it: it’s not the nutritionally perfect meal.

In this half-hour demo, I’ll show you how to level up your ramen using simple, shelf-stable, or dorm-fridge ingredients that make it actually good — and better for you, too. You’ll walk away with:

A concise shopping list

A few go-to "recipes" (more like assembly-instructions)

A belly full of ramen (veg and meat options — vegan next time if there’s demand!)

Where? My kitchen in DR 1030
When? Thursday, October 9th, 6:30PM - 7:30PM (the demo will only take 30 minutes)
Spots? Just 10 — RSVP fast!

No cooking experience needed. Everything will be just a bit more advanced than boiling water.

My hypoallergenic dog Oz will be there. If that’s a plus, great. If not, he’s happy to nap elsewhere.

name: Summer Dennis @ Kennedy Center
location: Amsterdam Hall - Walk to Kennedy Center
description:
Summer Dennis is an award-winning R&B singer known for her warm, welcoming vocal style that reflects a deep love for music. Influenced by legends like Lauryn Hill, Whitney Houstin, and Earth, Wind & Fire, Summer blends soulful expression with technical mastery. A two-time Wammie Award winner, she achieved national recognition when her single “Everything” peaked at #29 on the Billboard R&B charts. Classically trained, Summer is a versatile vocalist capable of performing across genres including gospel, R&B, rock, pop, and classical. Summer effortlessly covers vocal ranges from first soprano through alto and has over 20 years of professional vocal experience. In addition to her music career, she is a trained dancer and has spent over a decade exploring business development, with a growing passion for producing content for other bands and artists.

description:

This curriculum is designed with the unique dynamics of club sports in mind, including peer leadership, volunteer roles, team cohesion, competitive pressures, and limited oversight. It also aligns with university values and student development goals to support both individual growth and team success.

 

This workshop is Module 3 of 3, offered twice during the fall semester. If you register for the first session, please plan to attend all three modules:

name: The New Airwaves: An Exclusive Chat with Aaron Parnas
description:
Join the George Washington University College Democrats for an exclusive conversation with GW Alum Aaron Parnas. Aaron Parnas is a Democratic activist and independent journalist, with over 4.2 million followers on TikTok and hundreds of thousands more across other platforms. Aaron is working to create an accessible and truthful media platform made for the 21st century, bringing breaking news and analysis to a large audience. 

 

In this moderated conversation, we will be discussing the emerging role of independent journalism and digital communications, recent political developments, and what we as citizens can do to support our democracy. The event will begin promptly at 7:00pm, with the doors opening at 6:40pm. The event is being held in the Betts Theatre on the first floor of the University Student Center. Please RSVP on Engage so that we can ensure enough space for all attendees.

name: Multicultural Culinary Night - Camp Wellbeing
description:
Food has the power to connect us to who we are and where we come from, especially when we're far from home. Join us at our Multicultural Culinary Night with Health Promotion and Education, along with GW Dining, to explore this connection through food!
 
We’ll be making Kimchi Fried Rice together, and learning how to recreate the meal in your own dorm! This is more than just a cooking class; this night is about learning how to use food as a tool to ground yourself and stay connected to your cultural roots through food! This is more than a meal; it’s a celebration of identity, belonging, and the strength we draw from the places we come from. Come for the food, stay for the conversation, and leave with a renewed sense of what it means to nurture yourself from the inside out.
 
"Food is about history, and history is about identity. What you eat is part of your heritage, and it connects you to your roots. It’s a way to share stories, keep traditions alive, and maintain wellness—culturally and personally." - Marcus Samuelsson
 
This event is first-come, first-served!

name: Team First: Conflict Management for GW Club Sports Leaders - Module 2
description:
Module 2: Communication & Team Conflict Scenarios

 

Club sport leaders often juggle friendship, authority, and accountability within the same peer group—making proactive conflict management skills not just helpful, but essential. This curriculum is designed with the unique dynamics of club sports in mind, including peer leadership, volunteer roles, team cohesion, competitive pressures, and limited oversight. It also aligns with university values and student development goals to support both individual growth and team success.

 

This workshop is Module 2 of 3, offered twice during the fall semester. If you register for the first session, please plan to attend all three modules:

Session 1:

Module 1: September 21

Module 2: September 28

Module 3: October 5

name: Soulful Sundays: Meet & Greet Your Faculty-in-Residence (FiR) & Watch Netflix's High On The Hog
description:
Join the 1st Year (Drs. Cuellar, Dortch & Wright) AND Upperclass(Drs. Russ & Zhao) FiR's for dinner and conversation.

We will be watching High On The Hog: How African American Cuisine Transformed America  a four-part docuseries on Netflix which explores and celebrates black contributions to global food and culture.

The show considers how much of what we consider American cuisine today was influenced by African American culture, through generations of enslavement and the fight for equal civil rights.

We will watch one episode per month.

Space is limited, RVSP required.

name: HTWH: One of the Good Ones
description:
Hot Topics with Hailey is back! 👩🏾‍🦱🔥 We know you missed it. This time, we’re diving deep into what it means to be labeled “one of the good ones.” 🤔 From the model minority myth to Black excellence and respectability politics, we’ll explore the pressures on communities of color to conform in order to be accepted or seen as successful. Who gets to wear this label—and at what cost? 💭 Come ready for honest conversations and fresh perspectives. No respectability required. 😌✨ Join us Wednesday, 9/24 from 5:00 to 6:30 PM in the MSSC Lounge!

 

This program is open to all students of the GW community. Participation is not limited based on any individual’s personal identity, characteristics, or viewpoint, including but not limited to: race, color, national origin, shared ancestry, religion, political affiliation, sex, age, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status.

Postcards are a special way of connecting with people anywhere in the world. They’re small, easy to travel with, available for purchase at many museums/gift shops, and arrive to recipients quickly. They become tokens that are kept in families for years, and are an easy way to show someone you remember them. Join in this storied tradition and connect with others as you do so!

 

Yours sincerely,

CEAd Jorge

name: Movie Night in Georgetown: Jordan Peele's HIM @AMC Georgetown 14
description:
What would you sacrifice to become the greatest of all time?

From Oscar® winner Jordan Peele and Monkeypaw Productions, producers of the landmark horror films Get Out, Us, Candyman and Nope, comes a chilling journey into the inner sanctum of fame, idolatry and the pursuit of excellence at any cost, featuring an electrifying dramatic performance from Marlon Wayans (Air, Respect).

Former college wide-receiver Tyriq Withers (Atlanta, the upcoming I Know What You Did Last Summer) plays Cameron Cade, a rising-star quarterback who has devoted his life, and identity, to football. On the eve of professional football’s annual scouting Combine, Cam is attacked by an unhinged fan and suffers a potentially career-ending brain trauma.

Just when all seems lost, Cam receives a lifeline when his hero, Isaiah White (Marlon Wayans), a legendary eight-time Championship quarterback and cultural megastar, offers to train Cam at Isaiah’s isolated compound that he shares with his celebrity influencer wife, Elsie White (Julia Fox; Uncut Gems, No Sudden Move). But as Cam’s training accelerates, Isaiah’s charisma begins to curdle into something darker, sending his protégé down a disorienting rabbit hole that may cost him more than he ever bargained for.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hpEy0iOixb4 

SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 21st 

We will be traveling to AMC Georgetown 14. 

Will be meeting in the lobby Guthridge Hall @7pm. 

Movie Starts @8pm. We will be watching it in IMAX! Run time is 96 minutes.  

Tickets are on us. Your ride there and back in on us. 

Popcorn, Soda Pop, & Candy on you! 

First some, First serve. So RSVP Soon.

description:
Join CHA to hear from multisite clinic director and experienced physical therapist, Chris Gregorski! Come learn more about the day to day life of a physical therapist and learn more about the role of physical therapy in treating Chronic Health Conditions! There will also be an interactive Q&A section!
 
Chris earned his undergraduate degree in Molecular Biology from Clemson University and went on to obtain his Doctor of Physical Therapy Degree from Wingate University. His career in physical therapy has spanned various settings, including rural access hospitals, outpatient orthopedics, and athletics.
 
Since relocating to Washington D.C., Chris has successfully opened two clinics in Northwest D.C., where he treats a diverse range of conditions. Over the past five years, Phoenix Physical Therapy DC has grown significantly under his leadership, accommodating approximately 44,000 patient visits for a wide array of impairments.
 
Chris is particularly passionate about treating chronic health conditions. He employs a holistic approach, integrating advanced therapeutic techniques and personalized care plans to help patients manage and improve their long-term health. His dedication to continuous learning and patient education ensures that individuals receive the best possible care to enhance their quality of life (and to have fun while doing it!)

name: Statistics Graduate Student Seminar 2025 Sep 19th
description:
We are delighted to announce our first seminar of the semester by Zixuan Zhao. 
 
Date & Time: 9.19th (this Friday), 2-3pm

Location: Rome Hall 771 conference room

Speaker: Zixuan Zhao (3rd year Phd student)

Title:   Provable Detection of LLM-Generated Text via Watermarking: Statistical considerations
  
Abstract: The paper studied watermarking-embedding imperceptible statistical signals into LLM-generated text-as a principled route to provable detection. A general hypothesis-testing framework that (i) selects a pivotal text statistic and a secret key (supplied by the LLM to the verifier) to control the false positive rate exactly, (ii) provides a closed-form asymptotic expression for the false negative rate to assess power, and (iii) reduces the search for the most powerful detector to a minimax optimization problem is proposed. Applying the framework to two representative watermarks(including one used internally at OpenAI), the optimal detection rules are derived. In numerical experiments, these theoretically derived detectors are competitive with, and sometimes more powerful than, existing approaches. Results offer practical guidance for implementing reliable watermarking systems in modern LLMs.
 
Attendance of Phd&Msc students is strongly encouraged. Hope to see some of you there!

name: DC Art All Night: U Street Saturday
description:
https://districtbridges.org/events/art-all-night-u-street/



Art All Night is a vibrant citywide celebration of the performing and visual arts in Washington, D.C. This year, the event will take place on September 12 and 13, 2025. The festival showcases a diverse range of local talent and creativity, highlighting the intersection of art and business across various commercial corridors.

The event features a wide array of activities, including painting, photography, sculpture, crafts, fashion, music, dance, theater, film, and poetry. Both indoor and outdoor venues, such as public spaces, local businesses, and restaurants, will host these activations. Each participating neighborhood plays a role in corridor revitalization by activating public spaces, highlighting local artists, attracting new visitors, and driving increased sales for small and local businesses. 

On Saturday, September 13th we invite you to join us in celebration of the performing and visual arts up and down the U Street Corridor in Washington, D.C.

U Street Corridor or Greater U Street, sometimes known as Cardozo/Shaw, is a neighborhood in Washington, D.C., located in Northwest D.C. Centered along U Street, the neighborhood is one of Washington's most popular nightlife and entertainment districts, as well as one of the most significant African American heritage districts in the country. The area was largely built after the U.S. Civil War and with the arrival of the Washington streetcar system in the 1880s, the neighborhood development boomed. By 1920, the neighborhood was predominantly African-American and flourished as the "Black Broadway", the heart of African-American culture in Washington.

Students should plan to meet Dr. Dwayne Kwaysee Wright (FiR in Guthridge Hall) @7pm in the Guthridge Hall Lobby @7pm.

name: National Mall Pre-Qualifier Pickleball Tournament
description:
This tournament will take place on Saturday, September 13th at the Vern from 1:00 – 3:00 PM. Please plan to arrive 15 minutes early for check-in and logistics. This event is open only to GW students, and all three required forms must be completed ahead of time and they can be found on our Linktree. Registration is $15 per person and must be paid through the GW Portal. When registering, follow the steps carefully, select Purchase: Event Registration, and specify “GW Pre-Qualifier Tournament.” Payments can be made together or separately.

Teams can register with or without a teammate, and co-ed or single-sex teams are welcome. Players should have a maximum DUPR of 3.5 (intermediate level), ensuring intermediate players have a chance to shine. Bring your own paddle, and be ready for round-robin play with a time limit instead of points. The top two person team will advance to the DMV Invitational on the National Mall on Friday, September 19th at 12 PM. For any questions, please reach out to gwpickleball@gmail.gwu.edu or on IG @gwpickleball.

name: DC Art All Night: A Trip to Mount Pleasant
description:
https://districtbridges.org/events/art-all-night-mount-pleasant/ 

Art All Night is a vibrant citywide celebration of the performing and visual arts in Washington, D.C. This year, the event will take place on September 12 and 13, 2025. The festival showcases a diverse range of local talent and creativity, highlighting the intersection of art and business across various commercial corridors 1.

The event features a wide array of activities, including painting, photography, sculpture, crafts, fashion, music, dance, theater, film, and poetry. Both indoor and outdoor venues, such as public spaces, local businesses, and restaurants, will host these activations. Each participating neighborhood plays a role in corridor revitalization by activating public spaces, highlighting local artists, attracting new visitors, and driving increased sales for small and local businesses. 

On Friday, September 12th we invite you to join us in celebration of the performing and visual arts within the Mount Pleasant neighborhood in Washington, D.C. Located in Northwest D.C., the neighborhood is centered along a commercial corridor on Mt. Pleasant Street. Mount Pleasant is known for its unique identity and multicultural landscape, home to diverse groups such as the punk rock, the Peace Corps and Hispanic Washingtonian communities.

Students should plan to meet Dr. Deniece Dortch (FiR for Thurston Hall) @7pm on Friday in the Thurston Hall Lobby. 

PLEASE BRING YOUR U-PASS!! 

Schedule of events can be seen below.

name: Celebration of Textiles: Enduring Traditions
location: The GW Museum and The Textile Museum
description:
Join The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum for a special centennial edition of our annual Celebration of Textiles community festival! This year, we’re highlighting the enduring textile traditions of cultures around the world, with special performances and activities led by practicing artists and diaspora communities from the Washington area. Explore the world of possibilities for making clothing and textiles, enjoy cultural dance and music performances, and visit our centennial exhibition Enduring Traditions: Celebrating the World of Textiles to explore global traditions that continue to inspire textile communities today. 

 

Performances and Activities

Drum circle with Kimia Percussion Academy

Traditional Bolivian dance performances from Alma Boliviana 

Sheep and other animals from Leesburg Animal Park

Mending with GW Innovation Center

Exhibition scavenger hunt in Enduring Traditions: Celebrating the World of Textiles 

Try on "Qipao" dress designs from China

 

Artist Demonstrations 

West African indigo with Kibibi Ajanku 

Indian woodblock printing with Trisha Gupta Art 

Northern Caucasian and contemporary felting with Alla and Milana Borovskaia 

Lacemaking with Chesapeake Lacemakers Guild 

Spinning with Fluff N’ Nonsense 

Carpet restoration with David Zahirpour 

Quilting with Uhuru Quilters Guild 

Chinese embroidery with Embassy of the People's Republic of China 

Flax processing with the Fiber Garden Project 

Fiber exploration with Chesapeake Fibershed 

 

How to Participate

This event is free; no registration required. Stop by the museum anytime between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. to join the festivities.

name: Museum Resume Workshop Series: Session 1: How to Present Transferable Skills
location: The GW Museum and The Textile Museum
description:
The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum invites you to a multi-part professional development workshop series for students interested in a career in museums or cultural institutions. Each session of the workshop will focus on improving one aspect of your job application material. The series will conclude with a resume review with department heads from The GW Museum and The Textile Museum.

Join museum director John Wetenhall and curator of education Lori Kartchner for our first session, where we will discuss how to present transferable skills on your resume. All graduate students come into their program with valuable skills that are attractive to potential employers, even if previous jobs are not within the field you now seek employment. Learn how to best display these skills while they are fresh in your mind.

The museum will provide light snacks and drinks during the workshop. This series is open to all GW students.

name: SENIOR WEEK: Adulting 101
description:
As you step into the next chapter of adulting and life after GW, one skill can make a huge difference in your career and your confidence: salary negotiation.

Did you know the average person switches jobs 10 times by age 40? That’s 10 chances to negotiate a better salary, stronger benefits, and more flexibility—if you know how to navigate the conversation.

This workshop will give you the tools and confidence to negotiate your first job offer like a pro—even if you’ve never done it before. You’ll learn:

How to research your salary range

Consider the whole salary and benefits package

Respond to the salary offer

Finalize the agreement


Whether you’re weighing an offer now or just want to be ready when it comes, this session is a must-attend for any senior who wants to start their career with confidence. 

Seats are limited, so don’t miss this chance to invest in your financial future. Join us and learn how to confidently negotiate like a pro.

Simone Williams is an experienced U.S. immigration lawyer and partner at Williams Global Law, who has worked extensively with students, entrepreneurs, and investors navigating U.S. immigration pathways. 

During this session, Ms. Williams will walk us through a range of visa options available post-graduation — from work visas (OPT, STEM OPT, H-1B) to investor visas (E-2), entrepreneurial pathways (L-1), and green card opportunities (EB-5 and EB-2 National Interest Waivers).

Whether you are looking to work, invest, start a business, or explore long-term residency options, this session will provide valuable insights to help you plan your next steps.

 

Date: Thursday, May 8th

name: Agape Christian Fellowship and Bible Study
description:
This semester we will study key statements Jesus made in John's gospel about who He is and what that means for our lives. 
 
We will use an approach called "Talk the Word" that has been developed by the Scottish Biblical Society where we share the word as it would have been shared in the early church - simply talking together and speaking the word person to person, rather than reading.
 
So take a break from reading and join us for a time of Bible study, prayer, and fellowship.  We look forward to how God will speak into our lives as we engage with the Word and with one another!

This conference is the culmination of the GW Refugee Access and Resource Initiative. This initiative focuses on:

Identifying challenges and barriers to success for refugee and displaced students.
Creating a resource bank to connect support networks across the university and DMV community.

During this gathering, we will share our findings from a previous conference, hear from student and faculty advocates, and discuss ways to enhance university resources. Additionally, our committee will strategize and discuss actionable recommendations to foster a more inclusive environment.

name: At Your Cervix Film Screening and Panel Discussion
description:
YOU CAN REGISTER FOR THIS EVENT HERE!

In honor of Sexual Assault Awareness Month, the George Washington University Office of Advocacy and Support (OAS) will be hosting a film screening of the groundbreaking documentary At Your Cervix on April 28th from 6pm-8:30pm. At Your Cervix breaks the silence about how medical and nursing students learn to perform pelvic exams. Following filmmaker and sexuality educator, A’magine, the film exposes how students are often taught on unconscious patients without their knowledge or consent. Interviews with students, patients, doctors, midwives, politicians and advocates provide compelling and often deeply emotional testimony as to why nonconsensual and unethical pelvic exams on patients under anesthesia must end. The film offers an empowering solution that will revolutionize how pelvic exams are taught and performed in schools and clinics across the country.

Directly following the film screening, OAS will be hosting a panel discussion with A'magine Goddard (she/they) where they will discuss why these painful, disempowering and re-traumatizing practices persist, despite repeated news exposés and the fact that a more ethical, effective and empowering teaching method is well-established. To learn more about At Your Cervix, please visit https://www.atyourcervixmovie.com/. You can also learn more about A'magine Goddard and their incredible work as a sex educator, filmmaker, and advocate by visiting https://amaginenation.com/about/.

The George Washington University Office of Advocacy and Support (OAS) is a university office that provides trauma-informed and healing-centered confidential support to student survivors of domestic violence, intimate partner violence, sexual assault, and stalking. You can learn more about OAS by visiting https://advocacy.gwu.edu/.

description:

What started in 2011 with a few students and a big idea has quickly become one of the largest student-organized TEDx events in the United States and around the world. Each year, TEDxFoggyBottom is brought to life by over 50 undergraduate students at The George Washington University in Washington, DC who work to bring together some of the world's most incredible innovators, thinkers, and doers to inspire and collaborate with the Foggy Bottom community. We invite anyone in the DC community to join us for a day of learning, growing and disruption. 

Tickets for the event include the ability to watch 8-10 TEDx Talks live from Betts Theater, connecting with local non-profits, a $100+ swag bag, a free catered lunch, and more.

FAQs:

What can I drop off/swap?

> Small household goods, kitchen items, stationary and school supplies, and room decor! Items must fit on a tabletop and be lightly used, clean, and in good condition. If you wouldn't feel comfy picking it up, don't leave it! Still unsure? bring it by and we'll let you know! 

Is everything free? Do I have to bring something to participate?

> All items at the table are free! While exchange isn't required, it is encouraged to keep our selection lively and exciting :) If you can't bring items to this Pop-up, you can add them to any "Stop n' Swap" bins in Residence Halls or bring them to our next Pop-Up. 

When is the next pop-up?

name: STATE ORGANS: DOCUMENTARY SCREENING + LIVE Q&A
description:
STATE ORGANS: Documentary Screening + Expert Q&A Panel

 

💌 RSVP: https://stateorgans-gwu.eventbrite.com/

🗓️ Date & Time: Wednesday, April 23, 2025 | 6:00pm -8:00pm

📍 Venue: George Washington University University Student Center, 3rd Floor, Amphitheater

🗺️ Address: 800 21st St NW, Washington, DC 20052

 

Please join us for a screening and discussion of State Organs, a 2025 Oscar Contender for Best Documentary Feature and an eye-opening expose revealing a state sanctioned, billion-dollar transplant industry fueled by forced organ harvesting in China.

 

Produced by Peabody Award-winner Raymond Zhang with a score by Emmy Award-winning composer Daryl Bennett, the film follows two Chinese families in their 20-year-long search for their loved ones who have disappeared in police custody. Along the way, they uncover a harrowing government-run organ harvesting operation that has destroyed many thousands of lives.

 

With operatives of the CCP being arrested throughout the US, and the regime’s attempts to suppress Falun Gong throughout the world, this documentary is not only timely, but a vital educational film on a devastating and ongoing issue.

 

There will be a Q & A session after the film screening with expert panelists. Light refreshments will be served.

 

Panelists:

Jessica Russo, PsyD – Mental Health Adviser for Doctors Against Forced Organ Harvesting (DAFOH); clinical psychologist and faculty member; speaks on forced organ harvesting in China; DAFOH is a Nobel Peace Prize nominee.
Peiming Cheng - First known survivor of China's forced organ harvesting; woke up chained to bed with parts of liver and lung missing (The Diplomat / Telegraph)
William Huang – Former PhD candidate at TsingHua University; imprisoned and tortured in China for practicing Falun Gong; escaped to the U.S. in 2008; now a senior electrical engineer.
Jan Jekielek – Journalist and host of the show American Thought Leaders. Jan has interviewed nearly a thousand thought leaders on camera, and specializes in long-form discussions challenging the grand narratives of our time.

 

This event is co-sponsored by the End Forced Organ Harvesting Rotary Satellite Club.

We will use an approach called "Talk the Word" that has been developed by the Scottish Biblical Society where we share the word as it would have been shared in the early church - simply talking together and speaking the word person to person, rather than reading.
 
So take a break from reading and join us for a time of Bible study, prayer, and fellowship.  We look forward to how God will speak into our lives as we engage with the Word and with one another!

description:

We will observe objects such as Jupiter and Mars, as well as the Orion Nebula and the Pinwheel Galaxy. Participants will be able to download the Unistellar app on a smartphone or tablet to follow along with our observations on a personal device. As we need clear or only slightly cloudy skies in order to observe the universe, in the event of clouds or rain on the 15th, this event will be postponed until Tuesday, April 22nd, also at 9:00 p.m. on the Quad

name: Conditions inside CCB
description: The Criminal Justice Student Association is hosting a forum event in the spring in collaboration with DC prison abolition group Who Speaks For Me, focused on advocating for those impacted by the inhumane conditions of DC's Central Cell Block (CCB). CCB is the holding facility where individuals arrested in DC, regardless of the crimes they are accused of, are sent for up to 72 hours awaiting their initial presentation to the DC courts. Despite other states using less invasive systems to process and officially charge defendants, DC remains using an outdated, underground dungeon that strips people of their liberty and dignity as if they have already been convicted. The majority of incarcerated individuals in CCB have their charges dropped, yet they always leave with the baggage of their traumatic experience during their stay.

description:
Spring in DC is beautiful, and the Netherlands Carillon is no exception! 🌷 Join CEAd Jorge for a trip to the Netherlands Carillon to see thousands of tulips just steps away from Arlington Cemetery and Celebrate Earth Month with the Arlington Public Library, National Park Service, and Friends of the Mount Vernon Trail 🌎

 

💐 We'll take a moment to see and enjoy the flowers

🔔 Hear live carillon music

🇳🇱 enjoy stroop waffles courtesy of the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands

📸 and take in the beautiful sights of the District!

 

*Subject to changes based on weather. Engage will be updated if there is any change!

 

What is the Netherlands Carillon?

A carillon is a musical instrument made of fixed chromatically tuned bells sounded by hammers controlled by a keyboard.

 

The Netherlands Carillon is "From the People of the Netherlands to the People of the United States." This simple dedication on the Netherlands Carillon expresses the gratitude of the Dutch people for American aid received during and after World War II. The carillon itself symbolizes a friendship between the people of two countries, a friendship so rooted in common allegiance to the principles of freedom, justice, and democracy that it can weather any temporary difference of opinion.

We’ve created hike workbooks with reflective prompts, and we’ll provide food, snacks, and water to support you along the way.🤍🐛

name: Spring Semester Adam's Law Training
description:
In July of 2022, the Virginia General Assembly enacted a Hazing Prevention Training Requirement for colleges and universities. George Washington University (GWU)’s Office of Student Life already provides Hazing Prevention Training to fraternities and sororities; however, this new legislation (also known as Adam’s Law) expands training requirements to include all officers, members, and advisors of organizations with a certain type of membership process.

To meet the requirements of Adam’s Law, the Office of Student Life will be hosting Enhanced Hazing Prevention Training, which is mandatory for you to attend. If your organization has a competitive membership process, all current and prospective members, as well as officers and advisors of the student organization, must attend one of these trainings for the organization to remain active and in good standing with the Office of Student Life at GWU. GWU community members may attend these training sessions without prior registration.

name: Speaking Event with Congressman Brandon Gill
description:
Congressman Brandon Gill is the representative for Texas' 26th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives. Elected last fall, Gill is one of the youngest Congressman being elected at the age of 30. Born into a military family on a U.S. Air Force base, he grew up on a cattle ranch in West Texas. He later went on to  graduate cum laude from Dartmouth College with degrees in Economics and History. He previously worked as an investment banker and later as an analyst at a global hedge fund. Before his congressional tenure, Gill founded the D.C. Enquirer in 2018, aiming to support President Trump.

As a freshman congressman, Gill has advocated for policies aligning with President Trump's agenda, including securing the U.S.-Mexico border and reducing federal spending. Recently Gill introduced articles of impeachment against U.S. District Judge James Boasberg following a ruling that temporarily blocked a deportation order under the Alien Enemies Act. He also serves on the Delivering on Government Efficiency (D.O.G.E.) House subcommittee. Gill is married to Danielle D'Souza, the daughter of conservative commentator Dinesh D'Souza with one daughter.

name: Agency & Responsibility in the 21st Century
location: State Room at 1957 E Street NW (7th floor)
description:
The GWU Philosophy Club is excited to host our first annual conference for undergraduate students! Please see the full details of the conference below, including the call for papers as well as information on when the conference will be held:

 

The 1st annual GWU Philosophy Club Undergraduate Philosophy Conference will be held April 5, 2025 in the State Room (1957 E St NW, Washington, DC 20052). The purpose of this conference is to provide a forum for the presentation of philosophical work of undergraduates to their peers.

Papers are required to be of philosophical content, with the general theme being focused around questions of agency and negotiations of responsibility. Papers should be approximately 2,500-3000 words (8-10 pages). Electronic submissions are required and should be sent to the GWU Philosophy Club at gwuphilosophyclub@gmail.com by March 1st, 2025. Submissions should include both the full paper and an abstract of no more than 200 words. Please send your paper, prepared for review, as an email attachment. The attachment should be a single word document with title, abstract, paper, and bibliography. In the body of the email, please include the title of your paper, your name, and your university.

This is strictly an undergraduate conference, with only undergraduates allowed on the conference program. The single exception is the keynote speaker, Dr. Huaping Lu-Adler of Georgetown University.

For further information, contact Kalinda Milkie via email (kalindamilkie@gmail.com) or at the address below:

 

Phillips Hall, George Washington University

801 22nd Street NW.

Washington, D.C. 20052.

Mondays 8pm - 9pm

name: Spring Semester Adam's Law Training
description:
In July of 2022, the Virginia General Assembly enacted a Hazing Prevention Training Requirement for colleges and universities. George Washington University (GWU)’s Office of Student Life already provides Hazing Prevention Training to fraternities and sororities; however, this new legislation (also known as Adam’s Law) expands training requirements to include all officers, members, and advisors of organizations with a certain type of membership process.

To meet the requirements of Adam’s Law, the Office of Student Life will be hosting Enhanced Hazing Prevention Training, which is mandatory for you to attend. If your organization has a competitive membership process, all current and prospective members, as well as officers and advisors of the student organization, must attend one of these trainings for the organization to remain active and in good standing with the Office of Student Life at GWU. GWU community members may attend these training sessions without prior registration.

name: Trip to Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens
description:
Join CEAd Jorge and CC Kelvin for a trip to Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens in honor of Women's History Month!

RSVP Required due to limited number of tickets!

 

What is Hillwood?

Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens is the former home of Marjorie Merriweather Post (more below!). Hillwood is known for its large decorative French and Russian art. It houses one of the most comprehensive collections of Russian imperial art outside of Russia, a distinguished collection of French art from the 1700s, twenty-five acres of landscaped gardens and natural woodlands, and one of America's finest orchid collections (which will be blooming throughout March!).

 

Who was Marjorie Merriweather Post?

Marjorie Merriweather Post (1887 - 1973) was a businesswoman, philanthropist, socialite, heiress of the Postum Cereal Company, and alumna of the Mount Vernon Seminary (now GW's Mount Vernon Campus). As the heiress to the Postum Cereal Company, later General Foods, Marjorie Post was among the wealthiest women of her time. She exerted a strong hand in the business affairs of her company long before women appeared in major corporate boardrooms. Post also dedicated her intense focus to collecting French and Russian art as well as to making significant charitable contributions throughout her life, supporting organizations such as the Boy Scouts of America and the Mount Vernon Seminary.

description:
New Member Days was a requirement for all students who have joined a GW fraternity or sorority social organization. In these sessions, new members learned more about the history of fraternity and sorority life, and the importance of having that knowledge and respect for these organizations history today. The Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life found that the scope of this training needed to be expanded to include education around hazing prevention, the history of our organizations both nationally and locally, some of the outdated traditions that still exist, and how to build community with other chapters and councils.

Topics will include Red Bull’s use of digital platforms, viral marketing techniques, and how the brand has continuously pushed boundaries in the marketing landscape.

This event will demonstrate how brands like Red Bull make their presence felt in everyday life through unconventional methods. They go beyond traditional ads and tap into moments and places that people frequent, like events and pop-ups. It wraps up the week by showing the extreme end of "everyday marketing"—where brands become a part of the everyday environment in unexpected and impactful ways.

Join your faculty-in-residence Drs. Tamara Taggart, Donaldson Conserve, Dwayne Wright, Deniece Dortch, and Yanxiang Zhao for a professionally guided tour of the recently opened Go-Go Museum and Cafe.  

Experience the rhythm and soul of DC's unique musical heritage at the GO-GO Museum, where the infectious beats of the city's homegrown funk subgenre come alive! This immersive museum showcases the vibrant history of Go-Go music through interactive exhibits, rare memorabilia, and pulsating audio installations. Whether you're a music major or just looking for an authentic slice of the capital's cultural identity beyond the monuments, the GO-GO Museum delivers an unforgettable experience that connects you to the real, beating heart.

Friday, March 28

1pm: Meet at Madison Hall Lobby 

2pm: Tour starts (1 hour) 

We will meet in the Madison Hall (736 22nd St., NW) Lobby and take the Metro to the museum which is located in the Anacostia neighborhood of DC. You must bring your Metrocard or money to purchase a card. This trip requires a train and bus transfer (approximately 35 minutes of travel).

RSVPs are limited! 

***********

The Go-Go Museum & Café is the official site for the appreciation and study of go-go music (the official music of DC), history and culture from its headquarters in the historic Anacostia neighborhood of Washington, D.C. Go-go music is a brand of funk, R&B, hip-hop, and Afro-Latin rhythms created in the 1970s by "Godfather of Go-Go" Chuck Brown and his D.C. fans.

name: Decoding the Digital Footprint: How Social Media (Analytics) Shapes Consumer Choices
description:
Join us as we welcome Scott Jones from SCJ Marketing Consulting dive into how social media platforms collect and use data to shape consumer behavior and drive marketing decisions. Jones will explain the tools and techniques behind digital footprints, discussing how platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter analyze user data to create personalized marketing experiences. We'll also cover how companies interpret analytics from social media interactions, the impact of targeted ads, and how these insights influence what consumers see online. Attendees will gain a better understanding of how their own social media activity contributes to broader marketing strategies.

The goal of the event is to explore how the data we generate through daily social media interactions shapes marketing strategies, content creation, and consumer engagement and to showcase how social media and tech companies use data to personalize marketing and influence consumer choices, while educating students on the analytics side of digital marketing. Social media platforms are integral to our daily lives, and this session can showcase how our interactions, likes, and shares drive marketing decisions that we then encounter in our feeds every day.

name: Spring Semester Adam's Law Training
description:
In July of 2022, the Virginia General Assembly enacted a Hazing Prevention Training Requirement for colleges and universities. George Washington University (GWU)’s Office of Student Life already provides Hazing Prevention Training to fraternities and sororities; however, this new legislation (also known as Adam’s Law) expands training requirements to include all officers, members, and advisors of organizations with a certain type of membership process.

To meet the requirements of Adam’s Law, the Office of Student Life will be hosting Enhanced Hazing Prevention Training, which is mandatory for you to attend. If your organization has a competitive membership process, all current and prospective members, as well as officers and advisors of the student organization, must attend one of these trainings for the organization to remain active and in good standing with the Office of Student Life at GWU. GWU community members may attend these training sessions without prior registration.

name: XHUMA : Taste Of Africa 2025
description:
The African Students Association is thrilled to announce the return of its highly anticipated annual event—Taste of Africa! This vibrant cultural celebration promises an unforgettable evening filled with music, dance, fashion, and culinary delights, showcasing the rich and diverse heritage of Africa within the GWU community.

This year’s TOA theme is XHUMA—which means "to connect." XHUMA embodies unity, cultural exchange, and the creativity of our diaspora community based in the DMV. Inspired by the resilience of African artistry, which has been used to shape history, tell stories, and overcome struggles, this theme highlights how heritage, creativity, and community remain deeply connected—celebrating the strength, unity, and cultural evolution of African traditions across generations and regions.

TOA 2025 will feature an exciting lineup of performances, including music, dance, singing, and a fashion show highlighting African designers across the world.

Taste of Africa is also a feast for the senses! Enjoy an extraordinary dinner catered by some of the DMV’s best African restaurants, featuring authentic dishes from across the continent—North, East, West, Central, and Southern Africa.

✨ Cocktail Hour: 5:30 PM

🎭 Event Begins: 6:00 PM

🍽️ Dinner to Follow

🎭 Recommended Dress Code: African Attire | Dress to Impress | Cocktail Attire

We can't wait to celebrate with you at this year's Taste of Africa! For more information and updates, follow us on Instagram (@gwuasa) or email us at gwuasa7@gmail.com.

name: Public health movie night and discussion with Drs. Tamara Taggart and Tamara Henry!
description:
Through the lens of Chicago's devastating 1995 heat wave that claimed 739 lives, "Cooked: Survival by Zip Code" examines how natural disasters disproportionately impact marginalized communities, particularly the elderly and people of color. Filmmaker Judith Helfand weaves together stories of various climate catastrophes to reveal how structural racism and socioeconomic inequality determine who survives and recovers from these events. The documentary challenges viewers to recognize and address the invisible man-made disasters occurring in vulnerable communities before the next extreme weather event magnifies these pre-existing inequities.

 

Join faculty-in-residence Tamara Taggart and Tamara Henry for a showing of "Cooked: Survival by Zip Code" and discussion. There is a limit on RSVPs so register ASAP. You won't want to miss the pizza, popcorn, and eye opening film!

name: Spring Semester Adam's Law Training
description:
In July of 2022, the Virginia General Assembly enacted a Hazing Prevention Training Requirement for colleges and universities. George Washington University (GWU)’s Office of Student Life already provides Hazing Prevention Training to fraternities and sororities; however, this new legislation (also known as Adam’s Law) expands training requirements to include all officers, members, and advisors of organizations with a certain type of membership process.

To meet the requirements of Adam’s Law, the Office of Student Life will be hosting Enhanced Hazing Prevention Training, which is mandatory for you to attend. If your organization has a competitive membership process, all current and prospective members, as well as officers and advisors of the student organization, must attend one of these trainings for the organization to remain active and in good standing with the Office of Student Life at GWU. GWU community members may attend these training sessions without prior registration.

name: Fuenteovejuna at the GALA Hispanic Theatre
description:
Join Potomac's faculty in residence Profe Cuellar, and several student staff advisors on a visit to the GALA Hispanic Theatre to view Fuenteovejuna (description below). Please RSVP in advance, and prepare to meet in the Potomac lobby at 1:00 PM on March 2nd to travel to the theatre.

(Description provided by the GALA Theatre website)

Fuenteovejuna, perhaps Lope de Vega's most performed work, addresses the people's right to rebel against the abuse of power. Written in 1613 and based on real events, it tells the story of the commander of the town of Fuente Ovejuna, Fernán Gómez de Guzmán, subjects the citizens to suffer under the rigors of an arrogant, corrupt, and ruthless government. But when they find that power really resides in the citizens, they unite, take up arms, and confront authority with the battle cry of “What is Fuenteovejuna? “The whole town, together!”

Fuenteovejuna, quizás la obra más representada de Lope de Vega, habla de la rebelión del pueblo frente al abuso de poder. Escrita en 1613 y basada en hechos reales, cuenta la historia del comendador del pueblo de Fuente Ovejuna, Fernán Gómez de Guzmán, que lleva a padecer a los ciudadanos los rigores de un gobierno soberbio, corrupto y despiadado. Pero cuando el pueblo se cansa de ser humillado y encuentra que el poder realmente reside en la gente, es decide unirse, tomar las armas, y enfrentar a la autoridad bajo el grito de “¿Qué es Fuenteovejuna? ¡Todo el pueblo, a una!”.

name: intangible cultural heritage experiencing activity - chinese paper cut art
description:
Immersive Experience of Chinese Intangible Cultural Heritage

With exquisite craftsmanship and a deep appreciation for tradition, we sincerely invite you to participate in our upcoming cultural heritage experience event on March 1, 2025. This event will feature papercutting, calligraphy, and lacquered fan painting and will take place at The George Washington Museum & The Textile Museum, offering you a unique opportunity to explore the beauty of traditional Chinese culture.

Event Highlights

✂ Chinese Papercutting Art
Fuyo Hanfu Society is honored to invite Master Zhang Longze from Xiaoliu Art Studio, an expert in national-level intangible cultural heritage papercutting, to showcase this exquisite craft. You will have the chance to observe intricate papercutting artworks up close, interact with the master, and even try your hand at papercutting yourself. Experience the elegance of Eastern aesthetics as a simple red paper transforms into an intricate masterpiece.

🖋 Chinese Calligraphy Experience
Feel the charm of free-flowing brush strokes as you dive into the art of Chinese calligraphy! Learn the basic brush techniques, experience the rhythmic beauty of Chinese characters, and appreciate the profound cultural significance of Chinese script. Each stroke reflects the elegance and depth of Chinese culture, bringing you closer to this ancient tradition.

🎨 Lacquered Fan Painting Experience
A lacquered fan is a masterpiece that embodies centuries of craftsmanship. In this hands-on session, you will create your own lacquered fan, from designing the fan surface to painting and decorating it. Discover the unique charm of this ancient art form while showcasing your creativity through flowing colors. In the end, you’ll have a one-of-a-kind lacquered fan as a personal keepsake.

Reserve your spot now and immerse yourself in the beauty of Chinese cultural heritage! We look forward to your participation! @All

name: Fortress America: The Global Impact of Trump's Economic Nationalism
description: In recent years the world has witnessed a global trend towards conservatism, especially in the developed countries. It was under this background that the US presidential election concluded with Donald Trump becoming only the second president to serve two non-consecutive terms in the US.  Even before being elected, Trump did not shy away from vehemently advocating for an increase in economic protectionism, which was followed by his recent efforts to increase the tariffs on Mexican, Canadian, and Chinese products. Although many countries expressed their disapproval of these economic measures, Trump ventures further in saying that he will implement “reciprocal tariffs”. What are the implications of these policies to the global community? How will the other countries respond? How will America’s protectionism develop, and what can we expect from the Trump administration in the future? These are all issues centered to the panel’s discussion.

What can I drop off/swap?

A wide range of topics will be explored, including interfaith dating and family dynamics. This is a journey of thought-provoking discussions, and we hope you’ll join us!

name: What Heels Chicana/o/x/e Masculinity?
description:
Join Professor Francisco Galarte for a talk on Chicano fashion designer Willy Chavarria, whose Chicano-inspired clothing has garnered him the honor of CFDA Menswear Designer of the Year. Dr. Galarte engages in a case study of Chavarria’s first shoe design, the “Jalisco,” and argues that Chavarria’s Chicano-inspired designs challenge and redefine masculinity while exploring the intersections of race, sexuality, gender, and identity. He proposes that Chavarria's designs celebrate the heritage of Chicano fashion, promoting a radical politics of style that transcends conventional boundaries and encourages new expressions of cultural identity and Chicanx/o/a/e aesthetics.

 

This event is in collaboration with the Cisneros Hispanic Leadership Institute as part of the GW University Seminar Series Intersectional Masculinities: At the Junction of Multiculturalism and Patriarchy, curated by Dwayne Kwaysee Wright, Manuel Cuellar, James McMaster, and Desmond Goss.

name: UASA & Russia's War Against Ukraine Rally
description:
This year marks the third year since Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine. Please join us as we gather on the Lincoln Memorial to stand in solidarity with Ukraine.

Those who would like to walk with us should meet at the USC 1st floor at 1:00 on Feb. 22.

There is a mass gathering before the rally at 1:30-2:00. If you cannot make it before 2:00, please feel free to join us at 2:00 for the full event.

The rally lasts until 3:30, but you are welcome to stay longer.

Ukrainian flags will be distributed to those at the USC who would like one.

If you have any comments or questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to us at gwu.uasa@gmail.com

name: Planet Word Trip
description: Join Dr. Randi Kristensen and Blaze the Tra1l for lunch at Immigrant Food and a tour of the Planet Word Museum! Meet Dr. Randi in the in Guthridge community room at 11:30 where you will take the Metro to McPherson Square where the museum is. name: WiCyS GW x WiCyS Georgetown Networking Mixer
description: Calling all WiCyS GW & greater GW community members who are looking to expand their network in cybersecurity, computer science, national security and international affairs, and technology law and policy! 💻 🍎 We will be hosting a social networking event with WiCyS Georgetown on Saturday, February 22nd from 11AM to 1PM in District House B114. description:

We will use construction construction paper, white paper, markers, glue, and scissors so be sure to wear comfortable clothing and be ready to roll up your sleeves! Check our GroupMe linked on our home page for more live updates!

name: Spring 2025 Weekly Poker Session (Week 6)
description:
Come and join the Poker Club for our Spring 2025 weekly sessions! Table play occurs every Friday. Anyone interested at any skill level is encouraged to join.

 

The rule structure is Texas no limit hold'em. Everyone will receive a fictional cash bankroll upon registration ($13,500), and that money stays with you throughout the semester. Any profits and losses incurred during weekly play will accumulate, and players are ranked based on their bankroll value for end-of-semester tournament qualification. The tournament rounds will take place during the last two Fridays of the semester before finals.

 

We hope to see you soon, and please reach out to gwupokerclub@gmail.com or @gwupoker on Instagram with any questions.

name: Law Revue 2025
description:
Join GW Law Revue at 7:30 PM in Lisner Auditorium for our annual spring show! Tickets required and available at bit.ly/GWLawRevue
 
This year, the Law Revue show draws inspiration from popular films and television shows to bring the magic of the screen to the theater with a dynamic, action-packed performance starring GW Law students and faculty! Whether you're a fan of iconic classics or modern hits, this show offers something for everyone.
 
*All GW students may use code "IGOHERE" for $5 off*
 
[The annual Law Revue Show is a multi-act theatrical spectacle that combines music, dancing, and sketches for a live audience in Lisner Auditorium. GW Law Revue players come from a variety of artistic backgrounds. Some are seasoned performers, actors, and musicians; some are experienced stagehands, writers, and lyricists; and others are stepping onto the stage for the very first time.]

name: [insert here] Improv Show!
description: Join [insert here] improv for our SECOND show of the semester on FRIDAY 2/21 at 9 pm in the University Student Center Amphitheater (3rd floor). name: Agape Christian Fellowship and Bible Study
description:
This semester we will study key statements Jesus made in John's gospel about who He is and what that means for our lives. 
 
We will use an approach called "Talk the Word" that has been developed by the Scottish Biblical Society where we share the word as it would have been shared in the early church - simply talking together and speaking the word person to person, rather than reading.
 
So take a break from reading and join us for a time of Bible study, prayer, and fellowship.  We look forward to how God will speak into our lives as we engage with the Word and with one another!
